refuted.claim: HEADLINE: the leak is 'Rs 2.40 lakh a year'
refuted.why: The sale side nets NO sale returns and includes a bill the vault itself flagged as a duplicate the day before. SaleReturnDetail shows 837 Am Lower units returned in-window (831 of them by the parent 0000L). And SaleHeader 2002752.0001 is Duplicate-Bill.md's 'Hp3' — identical to the paisa to Hp2, 59 lines, keyed one minute apart — carrying 2,030.40 L of the Loose Milk. Net of returns: -Rs 1,85,029.74. Net of returns AND ex-duplicate: -Rs 1,70,271.92. The note contains the word 'return' exactly once, and it is about MAX(PurchaseCost).
refuted.correctedNumber: -Rs 1,70,271.92 (net of returns and the flagged duplicate bill), not -Rs 2,40,010.68 — a 29% overstatement

refuted.claim: §2: 'Jivo Wellness Pvt Ltd - Delhi, the parent (0000L) | 1 SKU | 1,108 units | -Rs 72,747.79 (30.3%)'
refuted.why: Gross of returns. 0000L bought Am Lower on FOUR identical 277-unit invoices (2025-09-21, 2025-11-08, 2025-12-25, 2026-03-02, same four line-rates 122.22/56.17/57.60/65.95) and returned THREE of them at the same rates — 831 units on 2025-09-21 17:16 (36 minutes after the invoice), 2025-12-24 and 2026-03-02 13:05. Net the parent kept 277 units.

refuted.claim: §2 headline: '74.6% of the leak is sold off-campus'
refuted.why: Falls out of the two base defects above. Net of returns and the duplicate bill: off-campus -Rs 1,09,809.22, campus -Rs 60,462.71, total -Rs 1,70,271.92. The direction (majority off-campus) survives; the figure does not.

refuted.claim: §2: 'The wholesale channel is a break-even channel because of the lines in this note'
refuted.why: The causal 'because' is unsupported. Verified: on Basement-counter cost the NGO's 85 non-leak SKUs earn +Rs 1,66,144.11 on Rs 55.06 L of revenue — 3.0%. Strip all 11 leak lines and the channel is still a ~2-3% channel against retail's 24.55%. The leak lines take it from ~2.4% to 1.03%; they do not make it break-even.
refuted.correctedNumber: Ex-leak-lines the NGO channel runs +Rs 1,66,144 on Rs 55.06 L = 3.0%

refuted.claim: §3: 'On 2026-05-07 ARY bought 2,800 L at Rs 65.00; on 2026-05-11 it invoiced 7,105.20 L... That single week is the whole milk leak' = -Rs 1,06,362.68
refuted.why: The purchase is exact (three lines 1,000+1,000+800 @ Rs 65.00 on 2026-05-07; Basement May WAC Rs 61.97 over 3,300 L). But 2,030.40 of the 7,105.20 L sits on SaleHeader 2002752.0001 — the bill the vault's own Duplicate-Bill.md (mined 2026-08-29) names as identical to the paisa to 2002751.0001, 59 lines each, keyed one minute apart. This note builds its most dramatic passage on those exact four bills and never mentions, links or excludes the duplicate.
refuted.correctedNumber: -Rs 75,970 on 5,074.80 L if the flagged duplicate is real; milk 12m WAC loss falls from -Rs 68,153 to -Rs 57,982

refuted.why: Each listed row checks out, but the table is silently ALL-TIME inside a note whose frame is 12 months (its rows sum to 22,105 L against §1's 13,605.20 L), and it silently omits every month with a sale but no Basement purchase: 2025-07 (2,500 L sold) and 2025-12 (1,500 L). 4,000 L — 18% of the milk it purports to account for — is simply not in the table, with no caveat.
refuted.correctedNumber: 4,000 L across 2025-07 and 2025-12 are unaccounted; the table is all-time, not the note's 12m window

refuted.claim: §4: 'on the Basement stream alone its month-matched figure is -Rs 78,863'
refuted.why: That is the ALL-TIME figure, inserted as a correction to a table whose other three columns are 12-month. Verified split: 12m window -Rs 96,362.68 on 12,105.20 matched L; pre-window +Rs 17,500 on 10,000 L; all-time sum -Rs 78,862.68. The note's number imports Rs 17,500 of profit earned BEFORE the window it is correcting.
refuted.correctedNumber: -Rs 96,362.68 on the note's own 12-month basis, not -Rs 78,863

refuted.claim: §4: the three-column spread is 'the honest error bar', giving 'Rs 0.71-1.60 lakh'
refuted.why: The month-matched column is not on the same unit base as the other two and the note never says so. Verified matched-unit coverage: Shubh Diwali Diya 3 of 72 units (4%), Red Label Tea 32 of 75 (43%), Mix Dal_L 187 of 236, Ginger_Z 400 of 480. The 'min 20 units' rule is applied to the 12m sale quantity, not to the month-matched quantity — so Shubh Diwali Diya's place in the surviving ten is decided by 3 units. Three columns on three different denominators are not an error bar.

refuted.claim: §6: 'ProductChildMaster holds one row per price revision' — the stated mechanism, illustrated with Am Lower's 52 children
refuted.why: Directly contradicts the note's own §5 on the same 52 rows, and §5 is the one that is right. A single purchase voucher buying three ChildIDs at three costs simultaneously, and nine ChildIDs selling concurrently in one month, cannot be a revision series. §6 states as settled mechanism the thing §5 spends three paragraphs disproving, and cites §5's own example as its evidence. (For Benadryl the verify pass's revision reading may hold — but the note generalises it and then applies it to a counter-example.)

refuted.claim: §6: 10,641 SKUs with both a ledger and a master row; 4,644 (43.6%) master-high; 33 (0.3%) master-low; 41 of 21,479 StandardCostPrice
refuted.why: 33 and 41-of-21,479 verify exactly. The other two do not reproduce on the query the note describes, nor on five variants I tried (raw PurchaseDetail; header-IsDeleted; line-IsDeleted; both; master-cost>0). Every one returns 10,696 and 4,678. Restricting to IsActive products gives 10,620/4,650 — still not the note's pair. Two figures printed VERIFIED that I cannot make the data produce.

refuted.claim: §1: 'Every one of the 24 carries ConversionFactor 1.000 with matching primary and alternate units, so none of this is a litres-versus-kilos artefact'
refuted.why: ConversionFactor is 1.000 on all 24 — but only 22 of 24 have UnitID = AlternateUnitID. The two exceptions are Loose Milk (primary Ltr, alternate Kgs) and Mix Dal_L (Kgs / Pcs). The disclaimer is factually wrong, and it is wrong on the single SKU it most needed to cover: milk is 28% of the reported leak and is the entire subject of §3.
refuted.correctedNumber: 22 of 24 have matching units, not 24; Loose Milk is Ltr/Kgs and Mix Dal_L is Kgs/Pcs

refuted.claim: §5: '9 of the 13 campus lines are outright profitable on an all-time cost basis' (Am Lower +7,491, Rk Container +8,955, Sz Candles +5,581, Scissor +1,674, Knife 12 +1,659, Sbe Party Popper +1,648, Girlish Woolen Pajami +1,038, Harish Hand Towel +972, Shakkar +317); the four negatives total -Rs 18,668
refuted.why: All nine figures and the -Rs 18,668 reproduce exactly — but they are SKU-TOTAL all-time figures, not campus-only, and the column is labelled 'campus lines'. For eight of the nine off-campus share is 0% so it makes no difference; for Am Lower — the largest — the +7,491 includes the 1,108 parent units at Rs 63.25. Campus-only Am Lower on all-time WAC is 402 x (229.83 - 102.64) = about +Rs 51,130. The label is wrong; the direction understates the note's own case.
refuted.correctedNumber: Am Lower campus-only on all-time cost is roughly +Rs 51,130, not +Rs 7,491

survivingClaimsRemoved: §6: '**`ProductChildMaster` holds one row per price revision**, so `MAX(PurchaseCost)` returns the dearest cost ever recorded for that code — Loose Milk 20 children from Rs 0.01 to Rs 65.00, Am Lower 52 from Rs 56.17 to Rs 340.00.' — the note's own §5 disproves this on the same 52 Am Lower rows, and I confirmed it live (one purchase voucher, three ChildIDs, three costs, same minute; nine ChildIDs selling concurrently in one month). The sentence should say the children are concurrent variants for apparel and general goods, price revisions only where the verify pass proved it (Benadryl). Leaving both readings in the same note is how the vault publishes a wrong number a third time.

§1: 'Every one of the 24 carries ConversionFactor 1.000 with matching primary and alternate units, so none of this is a litres-versus-kilos artefact.' — the second clause is false for Loose Milk (Ltr/Kgs) and Mix Dal_L (Kgs/Pcs). Delete the clause or restate it as ConversionFactor alone.
missing: Sale returns, entirely. The word does not appear in the note. SaleReturnHeader/SaleReturnDetail hold 1,911 docs / 3,309 lines, and 837 units of the note's biggest SKU came back in-window. Every figure in §1, §2 and §5 is gross of returns and nothing says so.

[[Duplicate-Bill]] is not linked, not mentioned, not in 'See also' — although it was mined 2026-08-29, one day before this rewrite, and it is about the exact four 2026-05-11 bills on which §3 rests its whole 'one transaction' story. 2,030.40 of the 7,105.20 L sits on the bill that note calls a probable duplicate.

The four repeating 277-unit Am Lower invoice/return cycles to the parent (invoiced 2025-09-21, 2025-11-08, 2025-12-25, 2026-03-02; three reversed at 2025-09-21 17:16, 2025-12-24, 2026-03-02 13:05, same four line-rates each time). The note reads these as 'intra-group clearance'. A reader needs to know it is a recurring bill-and-reverse cycle, which may be a stock movement booked as a sale, not four sales.

The `ary assort leak` help text still prints every claim this note deletes: 'purchase cost rose from Rs 45 to Rs 55... across all 16,105 litres', 'the price master still carried the old Rs 38.83 cost', '27 SKUs were leaking about Rs 3.06 lakh a year', and 'a subsidised price to a captive population may be deliberate' (internal/cli/assort.go lines 488-494). The note says the tool 'is unchanged and still points at the right rows' without warning that its own --help hands the reader back the refuted version.

Any action at all. The note ends on five caveats and names no next step, no owner and no date. It never asks the one question that decides whether this is fixable: is the NGO's Rs 47 contractual? It proves the price never moved across 22 months while Basement cost went 45 -> 65, and stops there. Compare the verify pass, which gives an ordered A/B list with owners.

A confidence mark anywhere. Every figure is stamped VERIFIED, including ones that are only as good as an unnetted, un-deduplicated sales base and the two §6 counts I could not reproduce. Under the vault's own rule these needed VERIFIED / ESTIMATED / NOT-CHECKED separation, which the note applies only to the -0.39% tax-basis line it borrowed.
